purpose: Run a Termux-owned command/status service without showing a Linux desktop, so a foreground headset app can exchange messages with Linux userland tools.
authority_boundary: Termux remains a normal Android app sidecar.
The command service is not Android shell, HOME, a broker authority, or a hidden watchdog.
Commands are allowlisted and scoped to lab diagnostics unless a product protocol is reviewed separately.
preflight: Meta Quest workflow is active for live device operations.
Termux is installed and can run Python or another small local service runtime.
The command service binds to device localhost only.
The foreground headset app has an explicit communication route to localhost or to a broker-mediated bridge.
start: Start the Termux command/status service on device loopback.
Foreground the headset app under test.
Send status, marker, and allowlisted command requests to the service.
Record whether responses continue while the headset app stays foregrounded.
status: The foreground headset app remains active.
The command service returns status JSON.
Allowlisted commands return stdout, stderr, exit code, and timing.
No X11 window or desktop surface is required for the service to operate.
stop: Stop the command service by recorded pid or visible service control.
Confirm no command listener remains unexpectedly exposed.
cleanup: Keep event logs as local run evidence only.
Do not commit real command transcripts, device paths, or package identities.
Promote only sanitized lessons or synthetic fixtures to public docs.
evidence: Process snapshot showing the command service without X11 desktop processes.
risks: Short foreground tests do not prove survival across sleep, reboot, or battery restrictions.
A real product route needs authentication, allowlists, timeouts, audit logs, and cancellation.
A headset app may need INTERNET permission or a broker-side adapter to reach localhost.
Foreground-service policy may apply if the sidecar must run unattended for long sessions.
